description.value: This longitudinal MRI study investigated neuroplasticity and cognitive changes in relation to altered cocaine intake by comparing cortical thickness and other neuroanatomical measures in cocaine users and matched healthy controls at baseline and follow-up.

spans.text: Thus, this longitudinal MRI study investigated neuroplasticity and cognitive changes in relation to altered cocaine intake.

value: We hypothesized CT/CSA in the six frontal regions of interest and cognitive performance to be lower in CU than in controls at baseline.
severity of drug use was expected to correlate negatively with cortical variables.
positive associations were anticipated between cognitive performance and cortical parameters.
we expected that CT and CSA are negatively affected by cocaine consumption and that those changes were more pronounced with higher amount of cocaine intake during the study interval.
cortical changes were also expected to be positively associated with cognitive change scores.

description.value: A longitudinal study with healthy controls and cocaine users assessed at baseline and follow-up, with a follow-up interval of at least six and up to 53 months.

time_from_intervention.value: a minimum of 6 months; interval duration: M = 19 months, max. duration 53 months

name.value: Longitudinal changes in cortical thickness in Decreasers

definition.value: Decreasers significantly increased their cortical thickness from baseline to follow-up in the superior frontal gyrus, middle frontal gyrus, and inferior frontal gyrus.

value: Our main results showed CT recovery in lateral frontal regions after decreasing or ceasing cocaine intake.

Thus, our analysis included the superior frontal gyrus (SFG), middle frontal gyrus (MFG; caudal and rostral middle frontal gyrus), IFG (pars opercularis, orbitalis, and triangularis), medial orbitofrontal cortex (OFC), lateral OFC, and anterior cingulate cortex (ACC; caudal and rostral anterior cingulate cortex).
A total of 38 healthy controls and 29 CU were included in this study

Subsequent Sidak-corrected tests for group comparisons at follow-up revealed that CT was significantly thicker in controls compared to   Sustained Users   in the SFG (P = .026), MFG (P = .008), and IFG (P = .047).

Subsequent Sidak-corrected tests for group comparisons at follow-up revealed that CT was significantly thicker in controls compared to   Sustained Users   in the SFG (P = .026), MFG (P = .008), and IFG (P = .047).

Applying mixed ANCOVAs significant group ∗ time interactions were found for CT in the SFG (F  = 4.16, P = .020,  η  = 0.12), MFG (F  = 4.64, P = .013,  η  = 0.13), and the IFG (F  = 3.23, P = .047,  η  = 0.10;  Fig. 3 ).
